title: The Debt I Paid Without Leaving My Name
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Last month, I was standing in line at the small pharmacy near my office when I overheard a woman apologizing to the cashier.
Narrator: [reflective] She was short on money for her son's medicine, and she kept asking if she could pay the rest tomorrow, although the cashier looked unsure.
Narrator: [gently] I didn't know her, and she never noticed me standing behind her, because she was too embarrassed to look up at anyone.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I could have simply paid the difference right there and told her it was from me, and she would have thanked me immediately.
Narrator: [determined] Instead, I asked the cashier quietly to add the missing amount to my own bill, and to please not mention who paid it.
Narrator: [honestly] The cashier looked confused, so I explained that if the woman knew, she might feel like she owed me something, and I didn't want that.
Narrator: [reflective] I walked out before she finished her purchase, so I never even saw her face clearly, and I still don't know her name.
Narrator: [with feeling] For a few days afterward, I kept wanting to tell my wife what happened, mostly because I felt proud of myself.
Narrator: [honestly] Then I realized that wanting to tell the story was exactly the danger my father warned me about years ago.
Narrator: [thoughtful] He always said that a good deed shared too quickly often loses its sincerity, because part of us starts performing for an audience.
Narrator: [gently] So I stayed quiet, although it was harder than I expected, because silence sometimes feels heavier than speaking.
Narrator: [peacefully] Now, whenever I pass that pharmacy, I think of her for a moment, hope her son is healthy, and then I simply keep walking.
Narrator: [sincere] I have learned that some good deeds are meant to stay between you, the moment, and Allah, without ever becoming a story you tell later.
